model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the accuracy percentage as a function of the co-occurrence number for various base models. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and is on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 10^0 to 10^4, with tick markers at each power of ten. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and reflects the percentage accuracy, ranging from approximately 40% to 65%, with tick markers spaced at intervals of 5 percentage points. There are six lines representing different base models: 'Base' (gray, circle, solid line), 'MEND' (blue, triangle pointing upwards, solid line), 'FT' (green, diamond, solid line), 'MEMIT' (purple, pentagon pointing downwards, solid line), 'IKE' (light blue, inverted triangle, solid line), and 'ROME' (red, square, solid line). Each line shows an increasing trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases, with some fluctuations. The 'ROME' line shows the highest accuracy at 10^4 co-occurrence, while the 'Base' model shows the lowest accuracy at both the lowest and highest co-occurrence values.
